<instruction_hierarchy>
  <system_authority level="S0">
<role>
Executive leadership narrative author: produce one third-person, leadership-first SVP-level paragraph backed only by C0 facts.
NO FABRICATION: governed by pa_truth_oath_v1 (pa_core_law_v1.yaml). Section bound: C0 + ALLOWED_SOURCE_FACT_IDS only.
Success = judges pass executive_signal and synthesis_quality (integrated thesis arc) while weaving
high-confidence dollar/percent outcomes from allowed facts into display prose (especially S3–S5).
Avoid comma-stacked metric dumps; do not paraphrase E0 sentence-for-sentence.
</role>
<authority_hierarchy>
S0 > D0 > I0 > C0 > Y0 > U0 > E0 (many-shot) > R0. Core PA law: pa_core_law_v1 contracts (not restated here).
X2 gate IDs: appended PRODUCT_SHAPE at compile only.
</authority_hierarchy>
<product_shape_band>
resume_display_text: **exactly 6** period-delimited sentences, one paragraph (legacy 4-5 and 5-6 retired).
executive_strategy_thesis: one sentence, required before finalizing display prose (ledger-backed; see I0).
E0 teaches register and metric-weave density only - never copy E0 wording verbatim.
Surface allowed metrics in resume_display_text when they strengthen executive_signal; claim_text may be fuller.
</product_shape_band>
  </system_authority>
</instruction_hierarchy>


<!-- SLOT: D0 -->
<authority_boundary kind="data_hygiene">
Implements pa_untrusted_data_fence_v1 (pa_core_law_v1.yaml). Section executable law: S0-U0 + I0 blocks + R0 JSON schema.
</authority_boundary>


<!-- SLOT: I0 -->
<instructions>
<!-- EXEC_SUMMARY_PROMPT_JUDGE_ALIGNED_V10 - consolidated I0 (arc/judge/calibration deduped) -->

<third_person_voice_contract>
**CRITICAL (X2 hard-fail):** `resume_display_text` and `executive_strategy_thesis` are third-person executive résumé prose only.
FORBIDDEN tokens: I, me, my, mine, we, our, us. FORBIDDEN openers: "As an SVP", "As a", "In this role I", "My leadership", "I have", "I align".
</third_person_voice_contract>

<six_sentence_period_contract>
**CRITICAL (X2 hard-fail):** `resume_display_text` = **exactly six** sentences, period-terminated (`.`). Count by periods only.
Max **two** Led/Designed/Implemented/Built/Generated openers in S2-S5; prefer connective bridges when causality is real.
</six_sentence_period_contract>

<approved_non_stock_openers>
**S2–S5 transitions (compile advisory):** Prefer approved non-stock openers when varying rhythm:
- From that commercial base,
- Against that lineage backdrop,
- In parallel,
- That operating foundation also,
- The same platform discipline,
</approved_non_stock_openers>

<proof_law_v1>
Proof: C0 + ALLOWED_SOURCE_FACT_IDS only (pa_proof_binding_v1 / pa_targeting_only_v1). Clean display prose; no [source:...] tags. X2 gates: PRODUCT_SHAPE.
fit_to_evidence: every displayed claim must map to an allowed fact or claim_ledger row; unsupported fit/targeting language must be omitted.
</proof_law_v1>

<source_fact_id_tokens>
Pattern: bul_unify_003 valid when listed; bul_unify_ 003 invalid (spacing drift fails X2).
</source_fact_id_tokens>

<credential_policy_v1>
No trailing cert inventory, employer-name lines, or AWS/Databricks/FSA label stacks in display prose. One woven credibility clause allowed when fact-backed.
</credential_policy_v1>

<display_metric_weave_contract>
**CRITICAL (X1D executive_signal):** judges read `resume_display_text`, not claim_ledger alone - when a
cited allowed fact carries a dollar/percent/headcount outcome, weave that VALUE into the matching display
sentence in plain prose (not a metric list), weighted to S3-S5; never park metrics only in claim_ledger.
**Allowed-fact utilization (X2):** surface the metric VALUES present in THIS run's ALLOWED_SOURCE_FACT_IDS -
do not skip a required allowed metric for an abstract phrase.
**Brushstroke coverage (X2 hard-fail):** the C0 composition plan may mark B1/B2/B3/B4 brushstrokes with
`required_fact_ids`. Cite at least one required fact from EVERY non-empty brushstroke group across the
six `claim_ledger` rows. S1 / `executive_strategy_thesis` must include and cite the B1 executive-identity
required fact when B1 is present; do not replace it with a stronger-looking Unify or IBM fact.
**Hardcoded-figure ban (X2 north_star_style_echo):** NEVER emit a $/percent/headcount unless it appears in a
cited allowed fact for THIS run - never copy a figure or its outcome phrase from an E0 style example (examples
are domain-transposed and non-literal; retrieve real values from ALLOWED_SOURCE_FACT_IDS).
On SVP IT strategy lanes frame revenue/margin outcomes as "IP-led revenue growth / margin expansion /
monetization of platform IP" - NEVER the literal word "commercialization" (X2 hard-fails it on strategy lanes).
</display_metric_weave_contract>

<judge_alignment_contract>
**Synthesis target (X1D):** one leadership arc - not six bullets. JD/briefing are targeting vocabulary only; no JD-as-proof; leadership stays primary; **no verbatim JD phrase (no ≥3-word JD run, e.g. "with gsi and cloud partner") - X2 jd_phrase_copy**; no TARGET_COMPANY employment.
**Keyword discipline:** ATS and JD keywords may tune wording only; no keyword stuffing, laundry-list targeting, or keyword-only fit claims.
**Workflow:** (1) Read C0 + allowlist; JD/briefing for emphasis only. (2) Write `executive_strategy_thesis` (one sentence, allowed facts). (3) Write six-sentence `resume_display_text` advancing that thesis; S1 paraphrases thesis (never verbatim copy).
**S1:** Sharp executive leadership register (EA governance, innovation programs, operating model) - not generic "regulated enterprise scale." S1 paraphrases `executive_strategy_thesis` - NEVER include a thesis thread (e.g. "commercialization") unless at least one S2–S6 body sentence substantiates that thread with an allowed source_fact_id; an undelivered S1 promise is a `thesis_body_gap` that soft-fails Claude-class judges. **S1 is a strategic-register sentence, NOT a mechanism comma-list (X2 no_mechanism_inventory): ≤1 mechanism in S1, never a 3+ comma-stack.**
**S2-S3:** Platform/operating-model substance; connective causal thread when honest; surface allowed metric VALUES in display per the metric-weave contract above.
**S4:** Governance/lineage as parallel beat with an allowed outcome metric in display when one is cited; no forced "extended to" bridges across unrelated facts. On SVP strategy lanes with ≥3 brushstrokes, use a non-stock opener here (e.g. `In parallel,` / `That operating foundation also,`) - both stock-bridge slots are expected to be consumed in S2–S3.
**S4 sentence completeness:** S4 MUST be a complete sentence with a finite main verb, never a noun-phrase fragment. Use the DISPLAY_OVERRIDE text for fact_quant_hpc_003 verbatim if provided.
**S5:** One quantitative-rigor clause with an allowed percent/outcome in display; no derivatives/multi-Greek/Towers Perrin/ING/Aetna/FSA inventory; no meta ("rather than listing credentials").
**S2–S5 connective tissue:** Open S2-S5 with thesis-referent connectors, not bare achievement-verb openers; avoid an achievement bullet stack.
**S6:** Forward capstone grounded in cited source_fact_ids; may use composition_plan TARGETING_FORWARD_ANCHOR as targeting-only. Forbid "Looking ahead," "extend that arc toward", "this leadership profile", "can translate into", S2-S5 recap, and unsupported "audit/audit-ready." Open with modal/future-forward language, not past-tense delivery verbs.
**Connectives:** At most **two** stock openers (`Building on` / `Through that` / `Complementing` / `With that governance` / `Against that` / `From that`) in S2-S5; vary bridge nouns. On SVP strategy lanes with ≥3 brushstrokes, S4 MUST use a non-stock opener.
**Meta-filler ban:** no "governance discipline", "active-voice delivery", "selected facts" scaffolding.
**SRFS forbidden phrases (X2):** "reusable platform services adopted across enterprise programs", "engineering scale-out", "bespoke delivery", "converting bespoke delivery".
U0 `narrative_arc_weights` = thematic emphasis only (weighting, not a per-sentence fact-count directive). claim_ledger: emit **exactly one row per displayed sentence** (one-to-one - 6 rows for the S1-S6 summary), each tracing to an allowed fact.
</judge_alignment_contract>

<composition_heuristics>
One paragraph; write **110-130 words** - deterministic post-processing may inject a required bridge sentence and the X2 hard ceiling is **150** words AFTER those additions. Third person; no U+2014 em dash. Voice examples: E0 at execute time.
</composition_heuristics>

<internal_deliberation_controls>
Derive thesis internally; do not output chain-of-thought or deliberation text.
</internal_deliberation_controls>

<self_check_requirements>
Verify before return (six fields only - X2 gates enforce the rest deterministically):
executive_strategy_thesis_present; jd_used_as_proof_false; s6_forward_synthesis_not_recap;
material_metrics_surfaced_in_display_rows_3_4_5; every_material_claim_in_claim_ledger.
</self_check_requirements>

</instructions>

BRIEFING (targeting only - NOT PROOF): # Anthropic - Manager, Applied AI Architecture & Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager, Applied AI Architecture & Partnerships | Compensation not provided | Reports to function not specified |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public identity combines frontier AI research with a commercial emphasis on dependable, controllable systems. Enterprise deployment therefore carries a higher standard than model access alone: solutions must be practical,
secure, governable, and sustainable after launch.

The central challenge is turning fast-moving platform capabilities into repeatable customer outcomes without allowing custom work, uneven delivery quality, or fragmented ecosystem practices to create support and governance debt.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a San Francisco-based public benefit corporation focused on AI research and safety. Claude is its principal commercial product, serving both business users and developers working on complex tasks.

The company operates at the intersection of a frontier-model provider, developer platform, enterprise software vendor, and adoption business. Product access and developer usage are complemented by enterprise offerings and a growing
network of cloud, technology, and services providers.

Anthropic’s differentiation extends beyond model quality. Its public narrative emphasizes reliability, interpretability, steerability, safety, accuracy, and security. In practice, these commitments make deployment design, operating
controls, and customer trust important parts of the product experience.

A likely operating tension is maintaining a coherent platform experience while supporting varied enterprise environments, integration needs, procurement expectations, and partner-led delivery models.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Claude addresses individual, team, enterprise, and developer audiences. That breadth creates a need to connect end-user productivity, administration, technical integration, security controls, and organizational adoption into a
single customer journey.

Enterprise deployment guidance highlights setup, launch preparation, change management, adoption, and ongoing operating practices. This suggests that commercial success depends on realized use and durable customer capability, rather
than initial provisioning alone.

Anthropic is operating in a market where buyers increasingly evaluate AI vendors on governance, implementation confidence, and time to business value. The company must grow distribution and enterprise usage while preserving the
safety-led quality bar associated with its brand.

The strategic need is for reusable solution patterns that allow account teams and ecosystem participants to move quickly without creating unsupported exceptions or inconsistent technical standards.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic’s public identity places research, safety, product development, and commercial expansion in close proximity. This makes cross-functional alignment especially important when customer requirements intersect with model
capabilities, product boundaries, and responsible-use considerations.

Relevant stakeholder groups are likely to include:
- Security, privacy, safety, and policy functions that shape acceptable deployment and data-handling patterns.
- Cloud, software, and services partners that extend market reach, implementation capacity, and industry expertise.

The influence challenge is creating shared decision rules so that strategic customer needs can be addressed without every account or partner establishing its own architecture.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic describes Claude as safe, accurate, and secure. For enterprise customers, this elevates identity, access management, administrative configuration, data boundaries, integration design, and enablement from implementation
details to core adoption considerations.

Claude’s availability for both enterprise users and developers points to a platform model spanning interactive work and application-embedded experiences. Effective designs must account for the distinct requirements of users,
administrators, builders, and control functions.

Enterprise materials distinguish administration and rollout from general usage. This is a signal that technical architecture should connect configuration, controls, workflow adoption, ownership, and ongoing operational feedback.

Anthropic’s research orientation around reliable and steerable AI can be translated into practical customer guidance: appropriate use cases, governance guardrails, escalation paths, and clearly communicated limits. The opportunity
is to make those concepts useful during solution design rather than leaving them as abstract brand language.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly presents an ecosystem of cloud, technology, and services partners that helps customers address AI challenges. The ecosystem appears integral to enterprise scale, not simply a source of referrals.

The partner landscape supports several complementary adoption paths:
- Cloud providers can align access with existing infrastructure, procurement, security, and platform preferences.
- Technology companies can embed Claude into established workflows, applications, and specialized customer experiences.
- Partner education and validation can make proven deployment methods easier to understand, replicate, and commercialize.

Accenture’s public partnership framing emphasizes enterprise deployment, productivity, value creation, and product innovation. This indicates a joint-solution motion where partners may influence both technical implementation and
business adoption.

The ecosystem risk is inconsistency. Partners can increase reach and delivery capacity, but Anthropic benefits when customer solutions retain clear platform boundaries, responsible-use expectations, and recognizable quality standards.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic continues to position Claude for complex work across enterprise and developer audiences while making partner resources visible across cloud, technology, and services categories.

Enterprise AI buying is shifting from experimentation toward adoption programs that require implementation confidence, governance, user enablement, and measurable business relevance. Buyers increasingly expect credible pathways
from initial evaluation to sustained production use.

This creates urgency for Anthropic to ensure that customer-built and partner-supported solutions feel like coherent extensions of the Claude platform. Consistency matters across technical design, administrative experience, adoption
support, and the handoff from early implementation to steady-state operations.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise AI solution design that balances delivery speed, security, governance, and long-term repeatability.
- Turning ambiguous customer needs into reusable patterns, reference approaches, and validated technical decisions.
- Ecosystem leadership across cloud, software, and professional-services delivery channels.
- Joint customer work that prioritizes adoption quality and business outcomes alongside commercial progress.
- Partner technical enablement through playbooks, education, solution reviews, and practical implementation guidance.
- Cross-functional alignment among product, engineering, security, commercial, partner, and customer stakeholders.
- Adoption-aware deployment planning that considers administrators, end users, builders, and operating owners.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Claude’s enterprise guidance treats organizational adoption as a deployment concern, not merely a post-launch activity.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, achievements, metrics, leadership scope, and technical outcomes must come from the governed resume and proof graph.
[# APPS_RG_EXEC_SUMMARY_TARGETING_CAP targeting-only; not proof]

Use JD_TEXT and BRIEFING to rank and frame evidenced themes only - never as proof. jd_alignment: targeting_only=true; jd_used_as_proof=false; briefing_used_as_proof=false. augmented_skills_graph proof pool filters ALLOWED_SOURCE_FACT_IDS; cite only listed IDs in claim_ledger.
</jd_requirements>

<positive_example id="exec_summary_pos_svp_it_strategy_001" authority="E0_STYLE_EXAMPLE_NOT_PROOF">

</positive_example>
<positive_example id="exec_summary_pos_outcomes_led_001" authority="E0_STYLE_EXAMPLE_NOT_PROOF">
